newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish car output slumps 26 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Turkish car output slumps 26 pct in Sept.

text.p: Turkey's car production dived by 26 percent to 18,540 last month compared to September 1995, on slack demand which further weakened on expectations of tax-free imports, the association of Turkish automotive industry (OSD) said in its monthly bulletin.

"The market entered a waiting period particularly because of the discussions over tax-free imports. As a result, domestic car sales fell by 25 percent from 17,800 units in September 1995 to 13,417 (last month)," the OSD said.
Car and parts producers as well as labour unions in Turkey's automotive sector have recently been angered by government plans to ease car imports.

A cabinet decree was prepared to allow Turkish workers abroad who deposit at least 50,000 marks for one year at the central bank to bring in cars with a maximum age of four years without paying customs duties.
President Suleyman Demirel did not approve the decree, but Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has told journalists the government was determined to go ahead with the project.

The OSD said total motor vehicle output fell by 10 percent to 30,336 last month despite production increases of between nine and 63 percent in commercial vehicles. Farm tractor production, the second largest item, leapt 42 percent from a year ago to 5,044 in September.
Leading car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi resumed production today after a two-week stoppage from September 24 due to sharply lower demand.
The OSD said total motor vehicle output firmed to 237,384 in January-September, up nine percent from the same 1995 period while car production declined three percent to 155,614.
It said car sales rose 7.4 percent from a year ago to 156,482 units in the first nine months of 1996 with the help of a sharp increase in foreign car sales.

Imported car sales tripled to 32,156 while domestic car sales eased eight percent to 124,326 in January-September, bringing the market share of imports to 20.5 percent, compared to only 7.4 percent in the same 1995 period.

Nine-month output surged 135 percent from a year ago to 1,789 in buses, followed by a 59 percent jump to 3,744 in midibuses, 57 percent to 19,148 in trucks, 43 percent to 36,306 in farm tractors and 22 percent to 13,983 in pick-ups, the OSD said.
